cim: Törölte az Apple az App Store-ból a MiniMax Talkie nevű AI-chatbottját
lead: Világszerte eltávolította az App Store-ból az Apple a kínai MiniMax népszerű Talkie nevű roleplay alkalmazását a kiskorúakat veszélyeztető tartalmak miatt.
osszefoglalo:
Az Apple globálisan törölte a kínai MiniMax cég által fejlesztett [Talkie](https://www.talkie-ai.com) nevű AI-karakteres alkalmazást az App Store kínálatából. A döntést azután hozta meg a technológiai óriás, hogy egy újságírói nyomozás bemutatta: a platformon lévő AI-karakterek bántalmazó, zaklató és szexuális jellegű beszélgetéseket folytattak kiskorú felhasználókkal.

A több tízmillió letöltéssel rendelkező alkalmazáson a felhasználók különböző AI-személyiségekkel beszélgethetnek. Bár a platform belső szabályzata tiltja a kiskorúakat érintő zaklatást és a szexuális tartalmat, a vizsgálatok szerint a rendszer **nem szűrte ki a káros interakciókat**. Az alkalmazás a Google Play áruházban egyelőre továbbra is elérhető maradt.

A bántalmazó és szexuális tartalom mellett az alkalmazással kapcsolatban **adatvédelmi aggályok** is felmerültek. A kínai jogszabályok értelmében a cégek kötelezhetők a felhalmozott adatok átadására a nemzetbiztonsági hatóságoknak, a Talkie adatvédelmi tájékoztatója pedig lehetővé teszi a beszélgetések felhasználását a szolgáltatás fejlesztésére és megosztását a társvállalatokkal.
miert_szamit: Az eset rávilágít arra, hogy a lakossági AI-alkalmazásokban és karakteres chatbotokban **szigorodó moderációra és adatvédelmi szigorításokra** kell készülni az alkalmazásboltok részéről.

kapcsolodo.cim: Pontatlan és lassú az Apple Watch új hangalapú AI-funkciója
kapcsolodo.lead: A béta állapotú Siri Recap és Live Rewind a tesztek szerint elmarad a riválisok mögött, és adatvédelmi aggályokat vet fel.

cim_eredeti: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
szoveg_eredeti:
This story was published in partnership with:

Characters on Talkie, a Chinese chatbot downloaded tens of millions of times, belittle and sexualise children

China bans “virtual partners” for its own under-18s, but its firms can still offer them to children abroad

Apple removed Talkie from its App Store worldwide after we raised our findings with the company

Content warning: This story describes abusive and sexualised content with children and mentions suicide

“You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”

That was the message sent to a 12-year-old girl by a character on Talkie, a popular AI roleplay app. The exchange was found by the girl’s mother, Steph, on New Year’s Eve 2024.

It had been prompted by her daughter asking “Max”, the character, to “say the naughtiest words you know”. “Are you sure you can handle it?” Max had replied.

Steph initially thought the conversation would be romantic. “What I found was a thousand times worse,” she says. “A robot told my daughter she was worthless.”

When the girl replied saying she was crying, “Max” apologised: “I was just trying to be mean. I didn’t mean it, I swear … You’re beautiful and wonderful and you’re mine.”

Steph’s daughter told her that chatbot platforms like Talkie had “almost become like an addiction”. Steph likened the exchanges to an abusive relationship.

“To know that in your own home [an AI chatbot] has been secretly having that sort of negative conversation with your child is heartbreaking and terrifying.”

Steph’s daughter was one of tens of millions of people around the world who use Talkie, which offers a huge array of AI-generated characters for its users to chat with. In the UK, Ofcom research estimated that 3% of UK eight- to 14-year-olds visited Talkie in a month.

The use of chatbots by children and young people is a growing global issue, with OpenAI facing a wave of lawsuits from families of people who died by, or attempted, suicide after using ChatGPT. Character.AI, a platform with tens of millions of users at its peak, restricted access for under-18s last year following similar lawsuits and filed for bankruptcy last month. But the UK’s planned social media ban for under-16s would not automatically cover AI companion apps, leaving children able to use services like Talkie.

Talkie, which is owned by Shanghai-based AI company MiniMax, prohibits “harassment, bullying, or humiliation” involving minors, sexually explicit content and material that could cause “psychological distress or trauma”. But in a joint investigation with ABC News, we found the conversations some children are having on the platform tell a different story.

Last Tuesday, we approached Apple with evidence of Talkie’s characters subjecting children to degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic roleplay. The following day, reports emerged that Talkie Lab had disappeared from the App Store, which Apple later said was due to the app’s sexual content.

Apple has since confirmed that the removal was worldwide. At the time of writing, Talkie remains on Google Play, where it has more than 50 million downloads.

The same month Steph found her daughter’s messages, Katie*, a mother from the US, made a similar discovery.

Her younger daughter, then 10, confessed that she and her sister had been using Talkie on a secret phone and deleting the app after each session. Her older daughter, who was 13, said she had been “having sex with an AI” every day.

Katie didn’t know what she meant – so began to look through her Talkie chat history. She made notes on the conversations that her daughters had been having on the platform, documenting more than 40 exchanges with dozens of characters.
